thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] runtime-pool-3 (us-west-2) observed repeated OOMs and CUDA failures across paged-attention allocator instances. 12 nodes flapped in the last 18m, auto-evict tried and failed on 5 nodes. Please triage. 

Alex M: seeing a bunch of `cudaErrorLaunchFailure` in node logs + `OOM killed process runtime-worker` — looks like slow memory creep in KV / paged allocator. stack traces point at attention paging codepath. 

Priya S: confirming logs: 
```
# dmesg excerpt
[120045.123456] Out of memory: Killed process 25432 (runtime-worker) total_vm:3456789kB, anon_rss:2345678kB
[120045.123462] [drm] GPU hang: scheduling timeout
[120046.000000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3d:00): 31, Ch 00000001, GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

Josh K: grafana: https://grafana.redwood/runtime-pool-3/d/kv-paged/oom-spike?orgId=1 — error rate jumped from 0.2% -> 7.8% over 12m. p95 latency also spiked. link to node list: https://infra.redwood/nodes?pool=runtime-pool-3

ops-bot: Auto-eviction attempted on nodes [n-23,n-24,n-45,n-46,n-48]; compaction job kicked for n-23. Compaction failed (OOM during compaction) on n-24. 

Emma L: quick mitigation idea — reduce batch size and throttle concurrency for pool 3 via feature flags to limit peak KV allocations, and push a forced evict interval (lower threshold) to trigger more aggressive eviction. 

Alex M: agree. Rolling config change: reduce MAX_TOKENS_PER_BATCH=512 -> 256 and limit CONCURRENCY_PER_GPU=2 -> 1 for pool-3. Will apply via runtime-config endpoint. Also plan: schedule cordon/drain of the worst nodes and soft-restart runtime process to reclaim leaked slabs. 

Priya S: applying config now (will do canary on one node first). 
```
POST /api/v1/configs/runtime-pool-3
{
  "MAX_TOKENS_PER_BATCH": "256",
  "CONCURRENCY_PER_GPU": "1",
  "KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD": "0.65",
  "KV_COMPACT_TRIGGER": "on-demand"
}
```

Alex M: canary applied to n-46, monitoring. 

10m later

Priya S: canary looks promising — error rate on n-46 down to baseline, memory stable. rolling out to other nodes (staggered 2 at a time). 

Lucas R: noticed kernel OOM messages referencing `kv_cache_compact` in the trace. I dumped allocator stats: 
```
Allocator stats (n-24): total_pages: 128k, resident_pages: 118k, fragmented_pages: 42k, reserved_slabs: 920MB, leak_estimate: ~220MB over 3h
```

Josh K: starting node drain for n-24 and n-48 (they failed compaction). plan: cordon -> drain -> restart container -> run `kv-compact --background` -> monitor for CUDA errors. I'm going to sequence to avoid cluster-wide capacity loss. 

Tayla O: calling out customer impact: two customers in prod reported elevated error rates for embeddings and chat reranking (support ticket #INC-7892). SLOs impacted for ~600 requests/min during spike. Noted for postmortem. :loud_sound: 

Alex M: executed drain on n-24: 
```
kubectl cordon n-24
kubectl drain n-24 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
systemctl restart runtime-worker.service
/opt/bin/kv-compact --force --max-memory=500MB &
```

Priya S: n-24 restarted, compaction started — compaction log shows `evicted 34MB from kv pages` then `compaction paused: memory pressure`. compaction resumed after restart and completed ~45s later. 

ops-bot: Noting a spike in container restarts: runtime-worker restarted 7x in 22m across pool-3. Automated escalation threshold hit. 

Emma L: created short-term workaround: enable `KV_DRAIN_ON_IDLE=true` which will aggressively evict cold prefixes when load dips. pushing to all pool-3 instances. 

Alex M: after rolling config + drains, error rate for pool-3 down to 0.6% and p95 latency back near baseline. CUDA errors dropped to noise. customer tickets updated. 

Lucas R: open items for next shift: 1) follow up on heap leak root cause in paged attention codepath (assign to eng-runtime), 2) run full allocator telemetry export for last 24h and attach to INC-7892, 3) schedule a targeted canary with synthetic loads to validate compaction under stress, 4) consider adding an on-demand background compactor as persistent service. 

Priya S: creating Jira: RINF-4521 "Paged-attention allocator slow leak — investigation and fix" and attaching logs. 

Tayla O: handoff to next oncall: please monitor the pool-3 alert (alert id: A-1473) for 6h, do not revert KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD change until eng-runtime confirms. If errors spike >2% or container restart rate >5/min, re-cordon and escalate to eng-runtime lead. 

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated; impact: partial (SLA warnings for a small set of customers), mitigations applied: batch throttling, KV eviction threshold lowered, node drains+restarts, compaction run. Incident ticket: INC-7892, Pager duty incident: PD-3333. 

Alex M: leaving notes in runbook: /runbooks/kv-paged-attn-mitigation.md — added step-by-step commands and a checklist. tagging eng-runtime on the jira. 

Josh K: final checks — CPU/GPU utilization for pool-3 normalized, free memory on nodes increased ~18-25% after restarts/compactions. will keep an eye for 2 more hours then close the incident. 

Tayla O: acknowledging handoff. I'll take watch for next 4h and will escalate if anything recurs. leaving PS notes for support to update customers. :white_check_mark:
